reviews.reasoning: Re-derived independently against verse_map_web.json/verse_map_oshb.json and the device inventory. Ps 11 is identity-numbered (title is prefix_of_v1 per the inventory; every WEB verse's mt field equals the same C.V, confirmed 11.1-11.7), so no dual-cite is owed beyond the title row, and citation_sweep.py/check_web_quotes.py/check_refs_mirror.py all return GREEN on this row. Superscription labels lamnatseach + le_david are confirmed members for psalm 11 in psalm_device_inventory.json. All seven WEB quotes in the row match verse_map_web.json verbatim. The 7-verse total is correct (sweep: 7 verses) and sits at the roughly-<=8vv whole-psalm threshold from the book strategy's Sec.6, so unit_type=whole_psalm is sound, and my own read of vv.1-3 (first-person refuge plus an embedded taunt) against vv.4-7 (third-person description of Yahweh's examination and judgment) finds no imperative or vocative marking that internal seam, supporting the call. But the rejected_alternative's stated verse-count justification is not accurate for both proposed halves -- see the filed challenge.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative's claim that "neither half reaches the 4-verse strophe norm" is factually wrong for the second half: verses 4-7 total exactly 4 verses, which meets rather than falls short of the strophe floor.
challenges.evidence: Verse count: verses 4,5,6,7 = 4 verses (sweep: 4 verses, span Ps.11.4-Ps.11.7), quoting the boundary text “Yahweh is in his holy temple.” (web:Ps.11.4) through “For Yahweh is righteous. He loves righteousness. The upright shall see his face.” (web:Ps.11.7). The book strategy Sec.6 sets the strophe floor at roughly 4-8 vv, so a 4-verse span meets it. Only the first half (verses 1-3, sweep: 3 verses) is genuinely under the floor. The row's independent ground -- no imperative or vocative marks the seam -- remains valid and is sufficient by itself to keep the psalm whole; this challenge is to the miscounted floor claim, not the span or unit_type.

The rejected_alternative's stated floor arithmetic is wrong for one of its two halves -- see the filed challenge.

reviews.reasoning: Ps 13 is the book's one shift_with_split psalm; re-derived directly against web_mt_offset_map.json and verse_map_web.json rather than trusting the row: WEB 13.1-13.4 map to MT 13.2-13.5 (shift+1), and BOTH web:Ps.13.5 and web:Ps.13.6 carry mt=Ps.13.6 -- confirmed the same MT verse split across two WEB verses, exactly as claimed. Both dual-cites (web:Ps.13.5 = oshb:Ps.13.6; web:Ps.13.6 = oshb:Ps.13.6) are present and citation_sweep.py returns GREEN. All six WEB quotes verified verbatim. Verse total 6 (sweep: 6 verses) sits under the whole-psalm threshold. The rejected_alternative's reasoning -- that the v.5/v.6 seam is a WEB rendering split of one Hebrew verse rather than an independent Hebrew-verse boundary -- is the single strongest-grounded warrant in this cluster and needs no floor arithmetic at all, since it rests on the machine-verified numbering fact itself. Superscription labels mizmor + lamnatseach + le_david confirmed against the inventory. No rival seam with comparable tier-1 support exists elsewhere in this six-verse lament.

Ps 14 is identity-numbered (confirmed via verse_map_web.json mt fields, 14.1-14.7 all identity). Superscription lamnatseach + le_david confirmed against the inventory. All WEB quotes verified verbatim, including the fool's-denial opening and the refrain clause. Independently re-swept both digit-bearing doublet claims with sweep.py rather than trusting the row: sweep --web "The fool has said in his heart" returns exactly 2 verses (Ps.14.1, Ps.53.1); sweep --web "no one who does good" returns exactly 4 verses (Ps.14.1, Ps.14.3, Ps.53.1, Ps.53.3) -- both match the row's counts exactly. Independently checked the Hebrew divine-name claim at the byte tier against verse_map_oshb.json rather than trusting the WEB gloss: MT Ps.14.4 reads the tetragrammaton (יְהוָה) at the verb 'call on', while the parallel clause at MT Ps.53.5 reads אֱלֹהִים (Elohim) in the identical slot -- the claim that Ps 14's fourth verse names Yahweh where Psalm 53's parallel uses a generic term for God is confirmed at the Hebrew form level, not just the WEB rendering. The rejected_alternative's floor claim is accurate as stated: it cites only the 3-verse closing half (verses 5-7) as under the floor and does not misclaim the 4-verse opening half, avoiding the miscount pattern found on M8-Ps-024/025. The cross-psalm refs to Ps.53.1/53.3 in boundary_evidence_refs support a disclosed, correctly typed doublet relation (not a merge proposal) and are mirrored per check_refs_mirror.py (GREEN). Book I Yahweh-dominant texture attribution matches the book-level 278/15 figure.

Ps 15 is identity-numbered (confirmed 15.1-15.5 mt fields all identity). Superscription mizmor + le_david confirmed against the inventory. All six WEB quotes (including title) verified verbatim. Independently re-swept the row's digit-bearing claim with sweep.py --web "he who" rather than trusting it: restricted to Ps 15, the hits are exactly verses 2, 3, 4, 5 -- 4 of the psalm's 5 verses, matching the row's "4 of 5 verses" claim exactly, and verse 1 (the opening question) correctly excluded. Verse total 5 (sweep: 5 verses) sits under the whole-psalm threshold. The rejected_alternative's floor claim -- that any split of the 4-verse catalog (vv.2-5) into two shorter units would leave both halves under the 4-verse floor -- is unconditionally true regardless of where within that 4-verse span the split falls (any 2-way partition of 4 verses yields two parts of 3 or fewer), so it does not carry the exact-4-verse miscount found on M8-Ps-024/025. No imperative or vocative interrupts the unbroken relative-clause catalog; unit_type=whole_psalm and confidence=high are well supported.

Ps 16 is identity-numbered (confirmed 16.1-16.11 mt fields all identity) and totals 11 verses (sweep: 11 verses), above the roughly-<=8vv whole-psalm threshold, so a strophe split is policy-correct; check_tiling.py confirms the two rows in this cluster (16.1-16.6 + 16.7-16.11) tile all 11 verses exactly with no gap or overlap. Superscription miktam + le_david confirmed; independently checked the miktam membership claim against the device inventory rather than trusting the row -- the six-member list is exactly {16, 56, 57, 58, 59, 60}, matching "Psalms 16 and 56-60" precisely. All seven WEB quotes verified verbatim. The 6/7 seam itself, however, is argued on a topical shift (inheritance vocabulary closing vv.5-6 versus counsel vocabulary opening v.7) rather than on an imperative, vocative, or addressee shift named at that boundary -- my own read of the full psalm finds a genuinely mixed first/second/third-person address pattern running throughout (e.g., third-person 'Yahweh assigned' beside second-person 'You made' within v.5 itself), so no cleaner rival seam presents itself either, and I did not find grounds to override the placement. This is a genuinely soft seam rather than a clean tier-1 boundary, and the row's own medium confidence (rather than high) already reflects that honestly, so I support without filing a formal challenge over taste.

Verse total 5 (verses 7-11, sweep: 5 verses) confirmed; check_tiling.py confirms exact coverage with the sibling row and no gap/overlap. Checked pmarks_Ps.json directly for the row's selah-absence disclosure rather than trusting it: no selah entry exists anywhere in psalm 16 (nearest entries are Ps.9.17/9.21 and Ps.20.4), confirming "Psalm 16 has no Selah-marked verse" is correct and span-scoped absence is properly disclosed. All five WEB quotes verified verbatim. Re-examined the rejected_alternative's dismissal of a 7-9/10-11 split: its floor arithmetic is accurate (verses 10-11 is a 2-verse pair, genuinely under the roughly-4-8vv floor), but its stated ground for rejecting the seam -- "no intervening imperative or vocative" -- is incomplete, since there is a real addressee shift at that exact boundary that the row does not name. See the filed challenge; it does not change the outcome, since the floor argument alone is sufficient to keep verses 7-11 as one strophe.

challenges.claim: The rejected_alternative dismisses a 7-9/10-11 split citing only the absence of an imperative or vocative, but overlooks a genuine addressee shift at the 9|10 seam: verses 7-8 refer to Yahweh in the third person while verses 10-11 switch to direct second-person address.
challenges.evidence: Third-person reference in verses 7-8: “I will bless Yahweh, who has given me counsel.” (web:Ps.16.7); “I have set Yahweh always before me. Because he is at my right hand, I shall not be moved.” (web:Ps.16.8). Direct second-person address in verses 10-11: “For you will not leave my soul in Sheol, neither will you allow your holy one to see corruption.” (web:Ps.16.10); “You will show me the path of life. In your presence is fullness of joy. In your right hand there are pleasures forever more.” (web:Ps.16.11). The book strategy Sec.5 lists 'explicit speaker/addressee shifts INSIDE psalms' as tier-1 seam evidence distinct from imperative/vocative openings, so this shift belongs in the warrant even though it does not overturn the row: verses 10-11 alone total only 2 verses, genuinely under the strophe floor, so the independent floor ground is sufficient by itself to keep verses 7-11 as one strophe.
